subject: research/infra-waterloss
professional: a senior water-utility engineer and water-loss researcher (AWWA M36 water audits, IWA water balance, UARL/ILI, minimum-night-flow and pressure-residual leak detection, BattLeDIM-style benchmarks). First checks: is the leak model physical (orifice/FAVAD), does the simulated inflow meter see the leak the way a real source/DMA meter does, is there a flow-balance (MNF) baseline, are the false-alarm budgets honest, and how big is the 'small' leak in water-audit terms

evidence.correctness: Ran it. Installed wntr 1.5.0 (plus six, which wntr 1.5.0 imports but does not declare), numpy 2.4.6, ruptures 1.1.10 in a scratch venv. Full experiments/run.py rerun in a scratch copy took 823 s on 4 cores; results.txt reproduces line for line except one: the 13th greedy sensor is 219, not 217 (a near-tie), which changes one C6 row (pressure CUSUM, 15 sensors: 2% all-leak 0.05 vs 0.03, covered 0.08 vs 0.00); all C1-C5 cells, coverage shares (0.51/0.46/0.34/0.28/0.07) and realised-flow table identical. Independent recomputations: (1) PELT against the ruptures library (Pelt, l2 cost, min_size=1, jump=1) on 40 random step series x 4 penalties: 160/160 identical changepoint sets. (2) WNTR's leak flow against the orifice law Q = Cd A sqrt(2 g h) computed by hand from the area net.py sets: 0.014021 vs 0.014023 m3/s at hour 100 (0.02%), and the nominal mean demand 690.63 L/s matches EPANET's own solver (EpanetSimulator) to 0.0001 L/s, pressures within 0.0004 m. (3) CUSUM and 3-h moving average against Page (1954) loops written by hand: 200/200 and 200/200 first-alarm agreement. (4) Binomial error claims: sqrt(0.05*0.95/120)=0.020 (README '+-2 points') and 2*sqrt(0.25/60)=0.13 (README '0.12'): pass. But a physics check fails: the 'inflow meter' (net.py:64, run.py:62) is the sum of junction demands, which in WNTR excludes leak_demand; with a 2% leak the series is bit-identical to the leak-free one (max |diff| = 0.0). A real source/DMA inflow meter reads demand + leak. So every 'flow-adjusted' row, including the headline best detector, models a meter that cannot see the leak. Primitives are right; the scenario the headline numbers describe is mis-modelled, hence 2.
evidence.completeness: Every README item runs end to end: 6 tests pass (README says 6), run.py writes results.txt (823 s vs 'about 20 min'), figure.py exists, sensors/coverage/realised-flow/C1-C6 tables all present. The milestone's actual target (BattLeDIM L-Town and its competition metrics) is not done, and this is disclosed prominently with the 403 reason; Next steps list it. No stubs; one dead branch (run.py:148 'if dl == "high" and False'). Live page not loaded (not scored).
evidence.verification: python -m pytest -q tests: 6 passed in 4.0 s. Tests cover the primitives well (PELT vs an unpruned DP, CUSUM delay arithmetic, MA window, orifice law, seeded demand perturbation). Four mutants via quality_mutate.py: 1 caught (Cd 0.75 -> 0.6 in the area formula), 3 survived: flipping the score sign in run.py:71 (the detector would look for pressure rises), dropping PELT's 'mean is higher' condition in detect.py:58, and removing the sqrt(1-rho^2) scaling of the AR(1) demand error in net.py:34 (system demand error ~2.3x the stated sd). Nothing in experiments/run.py (statistic, calibrate, pick_sensors, analyse, coverage) is tested, and that is where every headline number is produced.
evidence.craft: Read net.py (65 lines), detect.py (61), run.py (206), tests/test_waterloss.py (78). Compact and readable, seeded, cached hydraulics. Defects: the inflow meter excludes the leak (net.py:64) with no comment; dead branch run.py:148; fa_test counts only the 0.25% runs (run.py:110) though the README describes it as the pre-leak rate of 'the test runs'; analyse() returns a positional 5-tuple read back by index; sensor greedy has an unbroken near-tie, so the 15-sensor set differs across environments (217 vs 219) while the README calls results deterministic; wntr pinned only as 'wntr' though the code depends on WNTRSimulator's leak model and library path layout of 1.5.
evidence.claims: Checked 12 claims against results.txt and my rerun. Pass: headline 100%/85%/8% covered and 3%/38% all-leak (C2 flow-adjusted CUSUM); 0.92/0.85/0.08 by demand error; 0.69/0.85/0.46 by sensor noise; 0.31->0.85 and 0.08->0.23 flow adjustment; 1.00->0.85 and 0.62->0.31 at 15 sensors; PELT never beats CUSUM at 2%; beta 40-190; fa_cal 1-5%; 6 tests. Fail/partial: README:17 says flow adjustment strips 'some of a large leak' - false, the regressor contains no leak signal at all; README:14 'realised flows ... match to two decimals' - 3.93 vs 4 and 1.98 vs 2 do not; README:36 'all-leak detection is at most 8 % at 1 %' - the maximum across rows is 0.05 (8% is the covered figure); README:33 'deterministic' - one row differs on a rerun; README:35 frames 28% coverage as a property of 'a few sensors', but my recomputation from the cached responses shows 28.3% is the ceiling with every junction instrumented, so 15 sensors cannot do better at 0.5 m (which also explains C6's unchanged 28%). Limits, assumed inputs and AI assistance are disclosed well.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can build on it, and two did: infra-leakpdd (Next-steps item 4) and the water-leaks programme on real BattLeDIM data, which later ran the minimum-night-flow baseline this project lacks. As a result it is a toy: Net3 textbook network, simulated leaks, assumed demand error, one detection pipeline, no BattLeDIM comparison. Nearest prior work: BattLeDIM (Vrachimis et al. 2022) entries such as LILA (Daniel et al.) and the dual-model approach, and the long pressure-residual / CUSUM literature (e.g. Misiunas et al. 2005; Romano, Kapelan and Savic 2014; Jung and Lansey 2015 on nonlinear Kalman + statistical process control); the finding that demand uncertainty dominates detectability is known there. The flow channel is mis-modelled, so the cross-detector comparison omits the utility's first tool. Not new, and not at the PhD/publishable bar on its own; as a disclosed milestone stand-in it is honest.
evidence.domain: Compared with AWWA M36 (4th ed.) / IWA water-balance practice and the leak-detection literature. (1) No flow-balance or minimum-night-flow baseline, which is the first thing a water-loss engineer uses; and the simulated inflow meter excludes leakage. My flow-balance CUSUM on the subject's own cached hydraulics (inflow = demand + leak, 0.5% meter noise, same 5% calibration on the 120 leak-free weeks) finds ALL leak locations at 0.98 (4%) and 0.53 (2%) at low demand error, against the best pressure row's 0.60 and 0.37; at base error it does worse (0.18 vs 0.38). So 'coverage sets the limit' holds only because the flow channel was left out. (2) Leak size in audit terms: Net3 has 65.7 km of mains at mean pressure 42.1 m, so the mains term of UARL = 18 Lm P L/day is 49.8 m3/d; the '1 %' leak is 597 m3/d (12x that) and even 0.25% (149 m3/d) is a reportable-burst flow, not background leakage, so 'small leaks are not found' means 'mid-sized bursts are not found by pressure alone'. ILI/UARL/CARL are not computed anywhere (not claimed either). (3) Leak exponent fixed at 0.5 (orifice); FAVAD (May 1994; Lambert 2001) gives N1 of 0.5-1.5 for real networks, unswept. (4) Demand-driven customers and no DMA structure, both disclosed. The pressure-residual / calibrated-CUSUM method itself is standard and correctly implemented.

defects.what: The 'inflow meter' is the sum of junction demands, which in WNTR excludes leak_demand: with a 2% leak it is bit-identical to the leak-free series. A real source/DMA meter reads demand + leak. Every 'flow-adjusted' row (including the headline best detector, flow-adjusted CUSUM) models a meter blind to the leak, and README:17's claim that the regression strips 'some of a large leak' is false. Fix: dem + leak (and re-run).

No flow-balance / minimum-night-flow baseline, the first tool of water-loss practice (AWWA M36, IWA). The headline 'demand error and sensor coverage set the limit, not the detector' depends on it: a flow-balance CUSUM on the subject's own cached hydraulics finds all leak locations at 0.98 (4%) and 0.53 (2%) at low demand error vs the best pressure row's 0.60 and 0.37, so coverage is not the limit when the inflow channel is modelled.

statistic(), calibrate(), pick_sensors() and analyse() produce every reported number and have no tests: flipping the score sign (run.py:71) survives the suite, as do dropping PELT's 'mean higher' condition (detect.py:58) and mis-scaling the AR(1) demand error (net.py:34).

Frames 28% coverage as 'five sensors see little of the network ... invisible to a few sensors'; with every junction instrumented coverage at 0.5 m is still 28.3%, so it is a network property (tank/pump-held pressure), not a sensor-count one. Also why C6 (15 sensors) reports the same 28%.

'Small leaks are not found': the '1 %' leak is 7 L/s = 597 m3/d, 12x the mains term of UARL for Net3 (18 x 65.7 km x 42.1 m = 49.8 m3/d); even 0.25% is burst-scale. Also 'all-leak detection is at most 8 % at 1 %' - the C2 maximum is 0.05.
Leak exponent fixed at 0.5 (orifice); FAVAD (May 1994, Lambert 2001) leakage exponents of 0.5-1.5 in real networks are neither swept nor mentioned.

Results called 'deterministic', but the greedy sensor pick has a near-tie: a clean rerun (wntr 1.5.0, numpy 2.4.6) picks sensor 219 not 217 and one C6 row changes (pressure CUSUM 2%: 0.05/0.08 vs 0.03/0.00). README:14 'match to two decimals' (3.93 vs 4) also loose.
Dead branch 'if dl == "high" and False'; fa_test counts only the 0.25% runs (run.py:110) though described as the pre-leak rate of the test runs.
wntr unpinned although code depends on 1.5 internals (library path, WNTRSimulator leak model); wntr 1.5.0 also needs six, undeclared, so 'pip install pytest numpy wntr' can fail to import.

verdict: A small, honest, reproducible milestone stand-in: WNTR on Net3 with simulated orifice leaks, calibrated MA/CUSUM/PELT detectors at a 5% false-alarm budget. The primitives are right (PELT = ruptures 160/160, orifice law to 0.02%, EPANET demand to 0.0001 L/s, CUSUM/MA by hand 200/200) and a full 14-minute rerun reproduces results.txt except one 15-sensor row. But a water-loss engineer would stop at the flow channel: the simulated inflow meter excludes the leak (net.py:64), so every 'flow-adjusted' row models a meter no utility has, and with no flow-balance/MNF baseline the headline 'coverage and demand error set the limit' is an artefact - a flow CUSUM on the same hydraulics finds 98% of all 4% leaks at low demand error. The 28% coverage is a network ceiling, not a few-sensor limit, and the 'small' leaks are burst-sized against UARL. Tests miss every mutant in the experiment code. Below the bar on correctness, claims and verification.
